title: Companion pack manifest (ws-companion/v1)
description: The pack.json of one companion pack. Readers ignore fields they do not know, so this schema leaves every object open except where the format itself is closed. A pack that passes this schema can still fail the dashboard's checks (file presence, sizes, image headers); use the import preview for the full check.

schema.description: The format marker. Any other value is refused.

id.description: The pack ID. It must equal the pack directory name and the marketplace entry id.

name.description: The display name. It must not be blank.

canvas.description: The logical canvas [width, height] in pixels.

autoMatch.description: Optional hints for the automatic pack choice: the pack scores higher when the running harness or model matches a tag.

persona.description: Optional character voice, read as untrusted quoted text. A persona that is malformed or too long is dropped without failing the pack.

quipLanguage.description: A language tag such as en or pt-BR.

voice_by_lang.description: Optional per-language voice overlays keyed by a language tag such as ko or pt-BR. The overlay matching the reply language is added after voice. A malformed entry is dropped alone; the persona and the pack still load.

head.description: The shared head: the egg-shaped head layers, the live eye layers, and the mouth rasters.

mouths.description: Mouth shapes by name; every value is a raster file name. Keys starting with eyeclosed- are reserved: they only register a closed-eye raster for older dashboards and are never drawn as a mouth.

hairs.description: Hair styles by ID. Each style holds back, front and acc layers.

poses.description: Poses by ID. stand is required; any other ID is optional and may name a fallback pose.

gestures.description: Gestures by ID. A gesture adds layers over a pose or replaces some of its layers.

expressions.description: Expressions by ID. An entry with a decal swaps the whole face for that raster.

props.description: Props by ID: floating items such as a drone or a letter.

fx.description: Effects by ID, drawn like props.

presets.description: Presets by ID. A preset may also pick an outfit, an eye set, attachments by slot, and palette colors.

scenarios.description: Scenario overrides and additions by ID.

outfits.description: Outfits by ID. An outfit maps columns (pose and gesture IDs) to body art that already wears the outfit. Each column also needs its entry under poses or gestures. A pack without outfits draws the layers under poses.

defaultOutfit.description: The outfit worn when no preset or setting picks one. Without it, the first outfit ID in sorted order is worn.

attachments.description: Attachments by ID: worn items such as a hat, ears or a tail. One attachment fills one slot.

slot.description: The slot the item fills: headdress, ears, accessory, tail, or a slot of your own (a lowercase letter, then up to 31 lowercase letters, digits, - or _).

bind.description: head moves the item with the head; body draws it with the body columns.

z.description: Stacking order; the default depends on the slot.

columns.description: For a body item: layers per column, used instead of layers while that column is drawn.

eyesets.description: Eye sets by ID, selectable in place of head.eyes. Each takes the keys of head.eyes.

registration.description: Optional reference points the authoring check compares outfit columns against: headAnchor and feetPivot as [x, y], and an allowed drift in pixels.

raster.description: A plain file name of a .png or .webp file in the pack directory: at most 128 characters before the extension, no folders.

channels.description: Raster channels of one drawn part. line is a fixed ink layer; the *Fill channels are neutral masks the runtime tints; detail is untinted.

fills.description: Tint masks by channel name: each raster is tinted with the palette color of its channel (skin, hair, eye, outfitPrimary, outfitAccent, or a channel of your own). A layer under poses or gestures still needs one of the fixed channels; an outfit or attachment layer may draw with fills alone.

palette.description: Colors by tint channel, each written #rrggbb.

closedL.description: Optional closed-eye sticker for the left eye, a full-canvas raster. While the eyes blink, the engine hides the sclera, iris, lid covers and lash and draws closedL and closedR instead. Both sides are needed; with one side or none the blink slides the lid.

closedR.description: Optional closed-eye sticker for the right eye. See closedL.

mode.description: Optional. It is inferred from the other keys: frames gives a frame loop, tinted channels give semantic-split, file alone gives static.

pivot.description: The joint [x, y] a motion rotates around.

motion.description: A named motion, or an inline track with oscillate or keyframes.

fps.description: Frames per second of a frame loop. A layer with frames needs it.

frames.description: Frames of a loop: raster file names, or objects of channels.

drawable.description: A layer that draws something: a raster, tinted channels, a frame loop, or the shared head.

kitDrawable.description: An outfit or attachment layer: a drawable layer that may also draw with fills alone, in the layer or in its frames.

column.description: An outfit column. Fields it leaves out, except layers, come from the poses or gestures entry of the same ID.

replaces.description: For a gesture column: the layers of the pose it swaps out.

pose.description: For a gesture: the pose it plays over.

fallback.description: The pose used when this one is missing a part; the default is stand.

replaces.description: For a gesture: the layers of the pose it swaps out.

effect.description: A prop or effect: a layer of its own, a list of layers, or both.

scenario.description: A scenario beat. It reacts to the events named by on, with optional guards and timed steps.

disabled.description: true mutes a built-in scenario of the same ID.

when.description: Guards. Only the keys below are accepted; an unknown guard fails the pack.
